claims.text: Technical debt is the extra cost a team pays on later changes because of how its code or setup is shaped today, compared with a shape that would make those changes easier; principal = one-off work to change the shape, interest = extra effort each change pays while it stays.

At stage-3, deploy/gitops/config-repo/envs/staging/api.yaml and envs/production/api.yaml differ in exactly two lines: line 1 (header comment naming the environment) and line 20 (replicas: 2 vs 3); the image tag (line 42), probes and resources (54-71) and the Service are identical.
claims.source_hint: tools/extract-code both files --tag stage-3, then compare: only lines 1 and 20 differ

claims.text: Lines 18-19 of api.yaml are the repository's note that replicas and the image tag are what differs between envs/staging and envs/production; at stage-3 the image (line 42) is equal in both and differs only between a deploy to staging and the next promotion; the memory limit is line 71.

With a full copy of api.yaml per environment, a change meant for both (memory limit, a probe) is made in both files; a change made in one copy and forgotten in the other leaves the environments different without anyone choosing it.

The move to a base and overlays (k8s.l2.config-repo-overlays, config-repo-kustomize/ at stage-3) is the principal of this debt; after it, a change meant for every environment is made once in the base.

Debt in a part nobody changes charges almost no interest; it becomes expensive where the team keeps working around it. Paying the principal is work too and pays back only through later changes in that area.

Taking on debt (e.g. a full copy per environment: quick to set up, easy to read) can be sound when delivering sooner is worth more than the interest, provided the team knows it took the debt and what each change will pay.

Debt is not the same as badly written code: well-written copies can charge interest through how they relate, and badly written code nobody changes charges almost no interest of this kind, because no change has to work around it.
Technical debt can live in configuration (manifests), not only in application code.

git diff --no-index compares two paths outside the index; on the two stage-3 api.yaml files it reports two changed places, each a - line then a + line: line 1 (header comment) and line 20 (replicas: 2 vs 3).
